task_message:
Case N05: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 441x441x156 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is finished.

**What I found and segmented:** a well-circumscribed, markedly T2-hyperintense (~3 cm) mass in the right pelvic/perineal region, with tapering bright poles running along a nerve/vessel track — the appearance of a peripheral nerve sheath tumor.

**Approach:**
1. `seg_open` + axial/coronal sheets to locate the lesion; confirmed the very bright central pelvic fluid collection was the bladder (separate structure) and not tumor.
2. Seeded the model with a single positive point on the lesion → 12.3 mL mask.
3. Verified the boundary with zoomed mask-cropped views in axial, coronal and sagittal planes; it closely followed the hyperintense margin.
4. `seg_refine` (12.1 mL) smoothed the contour without changing extent.
5. Reviewed intensity-based candidate proposals: accepted the two that were contiguous, tapering poles of the mass (C3, C4, +2.4 mL), rejected the anterior sheet and beaded tubular lines (C1, C2) as vessels/fascial planes.
6. Second `seg_refine` and a full five-slice-per-plane final review confirmed no lesion tissue beyond either end, a single component, and no stray inclusions; rejected the remaining candidates and saved.

Final mask: 14.4 mL, one connected component — confidence **medium** (main mass boundary is unambiguous; the thin polar extensions are an interpretive call).
